nodes.name: Has leadId?
nodes.notes: GATE WIDENED 2026-08-20 per Justin explicit sign-off: the hardcoded Bot-Fake-only restriction is removed. This now only checks that a leadId was actually passed in the request body -- a basic sanity guard, not a lead allowlist. Real safety now lives where Justin actually reviews before sending: Batch Approve's per-row UI (Send is only shown once a real graphMessageId thread is resolved) and the downstream "Has target?" node, which still refuses to send if no resolved email thread exists on the lead. Leads with no email on file are expected and fine -- they simply never get a Send button in Batch Approve (no_graph_message_id / no thread to resolve).

nodes.name: Get lead
nodes.notes: GET, not runQuery -- we already have the exact doc id from the webhook payload, no need to search. continueOnFail so a bad/deleted leadId lands here as an error body instead of killing the run; 'Pick reply target' below checks doc.fields directly and treats anything without it as not-found.

nodes.name: Create reply draft
nodes.notes:
Graph's createReply creates a DRAFT reply (pre-addressed to the original sender, subject auto-set to 'RE: ...', quoted original body already included) and returns the full message resource -- including id/conversationId/webLink, same reason workflow 33 creates-then-sends instead of calling /sendMail directly. Deliberately NOT setting the app's own subject here -- letting Graph's auto 'RE:' subject stand is safer for thread grouping than overriding it. continueOnFail so a bad/stale graphMessageId (e.g. it really did go stale across a folder move despite the ImmutableId header) surfaces as an error body instead of killing the run; 'Draft created OK?' checks for it below.

REAL RISK, still unverified as of this build: whether a /createReply + edited body actually threads into the same Outlook conversation the way a manual Reply does. Workflows 33/11 only proved the graphMessageId survives capture (and, for 33, the send/folder-move) -- this is the first workflow that actually calls /createReply against one of those captured ids. Needs a real live send against Bot Fake to confirm either way.

nodes.name: Draft created OK?
nodes.notes: Same $json.id ? 1 : 0 > 0 shape as workflow 33's 'Draft created OK?' -- continueOnFail replaces $json with {error:...} on failure, so $json.id is undefined and this coerces to 0/false either way.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ body: { contentType: 'HTML', content: $json.bodyHtml }, toRecipients: ($json.toEmail ? [{ emailAddress: { address: $json.toEmail } }] : undefined) }) }}

nodes.name: PATCH reply draft body
nodes.notes: Replaces the draft's body entirely with our HTML (the app's follow-up text), which also drops the quoted-original-message content Graph auto-included on createReply. Deliberate for now to keep this simple and match what the app's own manual mailto: follow-ups look like -- revisit if Justin wants the quoted history kept.

nodes.name: Send reply
nodes.notes: Graph's /send takes no request body, same as workflow 33's 'Send draft message'. Referencing 'Convert body to HTML'.item.json.draftId directly (not $json.draftId) since the PATCH node's own response may not carry it.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ text: "", attachments: [ { contentType: "application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive", content: { type: "AdaptiveCard", $schema: "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json", version: "1.4", body: [ { type: "TextBlock", text: "✉️ Follow-up Sent (reply)", weight: "Bolder", size: "Medium", color: "Accent" }, { type: "TextBlock", text: $('Build lead patch').item.json.company, weight: "Bolder", size: "Large", wrap: true }, { type: "FactSet", facts: [ { title: "Contact", value: $('Build lead patch').item.json.contact }, { title: "Follow-up", value: $('Build lead patch').item.json.label } ] } ] } } ] }) }}

nodes.name: Notify Teams - Follow-up Sent
nodes.notes: Same Power Automate/Teams webhook workflows 32/33 already post to -- reused as-is. continueOnFail so a Teams hiccup never blocks the webhook response (Firestore's already updated by this point).

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, leadId: $('Build lead patch').item.json.leadId, graphMessageId: $('Convert body to HTML').item.json.draftId }) }}
={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: 'draft_create_failed', detail: ($json.error || null) }) }}
